statement: (i) Show that $\\int_{0}^{\\infty}e^{-x}\\,dx=1$. (ii) By writing $\\int_{0}^{\\infty}x e^{-x}\\,dx$ as a limit and integrating by parts, show that it also equals $1$.
solution: (i) $\\int_{0}^{R}e^{-x}dx=[-e^{-x}]_{0}^{R}=1-e^{-R}\\to 1$ as $R\\to\\infty$. (ii) $\\int_{0}^{R}x e^{-x}dx=[-xe^{-x}]_{0}^{R}+\\int_{0}^{R}e^{-x}dx=-Re^{-R}+1-e^{-R}\\to 1$ as $R\\to\\infty$. So both integrals equal $1$.
hints: Introduce an upper limit $R$ and let $R\\to\\infty$.
